title: Glucose is dynamically regulated by time of day in humans and Drosophila
experiments_summary:
The study employed two main experimental systems: human plasma metabolomics and Drosophila isotope tracing.

**Human Study:** Plasma samples were collected every 4 hours over 24 hours from 14 healthy subjects. A targeted ion-switching LC-MS method measured 93 metabolites. Multivariate analysis (PCA, pairwise OPLS-DA 'one versus all' models) assessed time-of-day variability, pathway analysis was conducted using MetaboAnalyst 5.0, and rhythmicity was tested using RAIN and JTK_CYCLE algorithms with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) correction at multiple FDR thresholds (q < 0.2, 0.3, 0.4).

**Drosophila Isotope Tracing Platform Development:** Wild-type (w1118), fumin (fmn), and per01 mutant flies were maintained at 25°C under 12:12 LD conditions. Uniformly labeled 13C6-glucose (1 M) with blue dye was injected intra-thoracically (~31 nl/fly) into cold-anesthetized flies at 4-hour intervals across the day (ZT 0–20). Flies were allowed to metabolize the tracer for 1 hour before collection. Geotaxis and locomotion assays verified that glucose injection did not impair fly physiology. Metabolites were extracted via a Bligh-Dyer adaptation and analyzed by two LC-MS/MS MRM methods (ESI positive: 211 transitions covering 22 metabolites; ESI negative: 95 transitions covering 15 metabolites) using an ACQUITY UPLC BEH Amide column coupled to a Waters Xevo TQ-S Micro triple quadrupole MS. Data were processed with instrumental drift correction, blue dye normalization, natural abundance (NA) correction via Polly Phi, and enrichment calculation.

**Circadian Clock Dependence:** per01 clock-null mutants underwent the same 13C6-glucose tracing protocol as wild-type flies. Hexose isotopologue labeling fractions were quantified across circadian time and rhythmicity assessed with RAIN.

**Feeding Behavior:** Feeding rhythms of wild-type and fmn flies were monitored using the Activity Recording CAFE (ARC) assay over 48 hours at 21°C.

**Fasting Experiment:** Wild-type flies were subjected to either ad libitum feeding or a 4-hour fast prior to 13C6-glucose injection at ZT 0–12, with 12C6-glucose-injected flies as background controls. Background and NA corrections were applied.

**NMR Lipid Tracing:** Flies were injected with unlabeled or [U-13C]-glucose and 1H-13C HSQC NMR spectra were acquired to quantify 13C incorporation into lipid-associated spectral regions across circadian time.

**Glycogen Assays:** Total glycogen was measured enzymatically using amyloglucosidase hydrolysis followed by Amplex Red glucose detection and BCA protein normalization (5 flies/replicate, 3 replicates/genotype/time point). Glycogen-associated glucose isotopologue labeling (M+6/M+0 ratio) was assessed by DESI-MS on Bligh-Dyer polar extracts from fly bodies collected every 4 hours.

**Proline Supplementation Survival Assay:** Wild-type and fmn flies were pre-fed 15 or 30 mM proline for 5 days, then injected with 12C6-glucose at ZT 4 or ZT 16 on day 6, and survival monitored daily for 3+ days.

**Data Analysis:** Multivariate analyses (PCA and OPLS-DA) were performed in SIMCA; shared-and-unique-structures (SUS) plots compared model loadings. Univariate analyses used two-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD post-hoc and BH correction. Rhythmicity was assessed with RAIN and JTK_CYCLE for 24-hour, 20–28-hour, and 12-hour periods at q < 0.2. Product-to-precursor (phi value) ratios for TCA cycle steps were computed using Polly Phi and tested for rhythmicity with RAIN (p < 0.1 threshold).
